A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Surg-3M/SurgFM work. All 15 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F, support comparison. Pages 5–15 are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original SurgFM experiments and ablations in Tables 2–6, data-scaling results in Figure 5, and curation-model evaluations in Tables S1–S3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments, ablations, data-scaling results, and supplementary curation-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The curation pipeline, ConvNeXt/DINO-based SurgFM, augmented distillation, and SurgFM-Vid aggregation procedure remain unchanged. Section 3 clarifies the description of frame extraction without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 4194 Surg-3M videos spanning 35 procedures and the same classification tasks. Evaluation still covers Cholec80, M2CAI16, AutoLaparo, GraSP, CholecT50, and SAR-RARP50. Newly reported footage statistics do not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every experiment in Tables 2–6, including the self-supervised methods, downstream specialist models, and video-classification baselines.

E3.justification: Sampling remains at 1 fps, and Section 5 and Appendices C–E retain the same splits, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets. The revised dataset-size descriptions do not establish a changed experimental sample or protocol.

E4.justification: The backbone, self-supervision, and augmented-distillation ablations in Table 2 are identical. The pretrained/frozen-model comparisons and annotation-data scaling analysis in Figure 5 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The five-fold evaluation procedures and standard-deviation reporting in Table 2, Figure 5, and Tables S1–S3 are retained. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds duration and full-frame counts for the listed datasets, including 938 hours and 85M frames for Surg-3M. Its sampled-frame entry becomes 3.4M rather than the coarser 3M; this alone does not establish dataset growth. All model-performance results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The distillation objective in Equation 1, video-embedding aggregation in Equation 2, and their mathematical definitions are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The dataset, foundation-model, augmented-distillation, performance, and annotation-efficiency contributions retain their meaning and scope. Replacing the headline image count with footage duration supplies another size descriptor without changing the central claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations in Section 6 and limitations in Section 7 are unchanged, including explanations of pretraining benefits and the need to extend SurgFM to pixel-wise tasks and improve self-distillation.

D1.justification: Table 1 supplies additional technical dataset metadata by distinguishing full-frame counts from 1-fps counts. Section 3 explicitly connects 1-fps extraction to foundation-model pretraining. Curation instructions, hardware, hyperparameters, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 63 references and related-work comparisons are retained. Table 1 expands descriptive statistics for existing datasets without adding cited works or changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized edits in the abstract, contributions paragraph, and Section 3 emphasize video duration and clarify frame sampling. The section structure and remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 removes the Year column, adds Hours and full-frame counts, and explicitly labels the sampled-frame column as 1 fps. Its formatting and nearby text flow change locally; all figures and other tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves dataset documentation by distinguishing footage duration, full-frame counts, and sampled frames while retaining the scientific evidence. The benefit is limited by incomplete reconciliation: Table 1 reports 3.4M sampled frames while Appendix E still says 3.3 million, and the unchanged table caption describes frame counts generally as sampled at 1 fps.
